title: Council questions annual bus subsidy as service misses part of its route - Exmouth Journal
body:

        It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Councillors have called for a bus subsidy approaching £10,000 a year to be reviewed after hearing the service no longer covers part of its intended route. The funding was questioned at Exmouth Town Council’s meeting on Monday, September 21, when councillors discussed the 99E service and wider disruption affecting local passengers. Cllr Steve Gazzard said a weak bridge in Moorfield Road had prevented the bus from serving that section of its route and urged the council to examine its financial support. “We need to be looking at the subsidy that we give Stagecoach for the 99E because it doesn’t go to where it’s supposed to be going,” he said. Cllr Gazzard initially put the annual subsidy at £7,000, but Cllr Tim Dumper said the amount was higher. “Actually, the subsidy is rather more than you said, Steve,” Cllr Dumper said. “It’s something like 9,700 or something approaching 10,000 a year.” Cllr Maddy Chapman said the issue had already been raised at a previous council meeting, when town clerk Lisa Bowman had said she would look into it. “We do pay for that route,” Cllr Chapman said. Cllr Dumper said the matter had not yet been taken forward, but action was planned. The discussion followed his report on an Exmouth Transport Partnership Working Party meeting held on September 15. That meeting had been inquorate, meaning it could not take formal decisions. Cllr Dumper said representatives from Stagecoach, Great Western Railway and the county council’s public transport department had not attended. He also highlighted difficulties affecting passengers during road diversions associated with the Dinan Way link road. Cllr Dumper said concerns had been passed on from residents in the Rivermead area about reaching diverted bus services. He had undertaken to write to Stagecoach and the county council’s public transport team. Councillors also heard concerns about the replacement of Sunday and evening 99E journeys by the 98 service. Cllr Dumper said the 99E was useful to some residents travelling into town, although he acknowledged that the 98 could offer a better replacement for others. No decision to reduce or withdraw the subsidy was recorded at the meeting. Local government Exmouth Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading...
